messages.content: Explain plainly and precisely.
What is a variable?
A variable is a named storage location or binding used to hold a value that a program can read or change.

What is the difference between a fact and an opinion?
A fact is a claim that can be checked against evidence. An opinion expresses a judgment, preference, or interpretation.

What does ambiguous mean?
Ambiguous means that a statement or situation permits more than one reasonable interpretation.

Latency is the delay between an action or request and its corresponding response.

Ownership identifies which part of a program is responsible for an object lifetime and resource release.

What does deterministic mean?

What is an invariant?
An invariant is a condition that must remain true at a defined boundary or throughout a defined operation.

What is an abstraction?
An abstraction exposes the properties needed for a task while hiding irrelevant implementation details.

What is a precondition?
A precondition is a condition that must be true before an operation is valid to perform.
You are a C++23 specialist. Explain plainly and precisely.
When should std::unique_ptr be preferred?
Prefer std::unique_ptr when exactly one owner controls an object lifetime. It expresses exclusive ownership, is movable but not copyable, and avoids shared-reference counting overhead.
You are a C++23 specialist. Explain plainly and precisely.
Why can returning std::string_view to a local std::string be invalid?
The local std::string is destroyed when the function returns. std::string_view is non-owning, so the returned view dangles.
You are a C++23 specialist. Explain plainly and precisely.
What is RAII in C++23?
RAII ties resource lifetime to object lifetime: acquire in construction and release in destruction so cleanup follows scope automatically.
You are a C++23 specialist. Explain plainly and precisely.
What does std::move actually do?
std::move performs no move itself. It casts its argument to an xvalue so overload resolution can select move operations when available.

When is std::expected useful in C++23?
std::expected is useful when failure is an ordinary typed outcome and callers should handle either a value or an error without exceptions.

What is the main design risk of std::shared_ptr?
The main risk is unclear ownership. It also adds reference-counting cost and can leak cycles unless weak references break them.

std::span communicates a non-owning contiguous view while carrying its element count, avoiding separate pointer-and-size parameters.

Undefined behavior means the C++ standard imposes no requirements after the invalid operation occurs; observed results are not reliable guarantees.

[[nodiscard]] requests a diagnostic when an important return value is ignored, helping catch discarded errors and results.

std::jthread joins automatically at destruction and integrates stop-token cancellation, reducing lifetime and shutdown mistakes.

When is std::pmr useful?
std::pmr is useful when allocation strategy must be selected at runtime or many short-lived allocations should share an arena-like memory resource.

Identify the root cause and smallest safe C++23 repair. Explain plainly and precisely.
Fix: std::string_view f(){ std::string s="x"; return s; }
Return an owning std::string: `std::string f(){ return "x"; }`. The original view referred to storage destroyed at function exit.
Identify the root cause and smallest safe C++23 repair. Explain plainly and precisely.
Only one subsystem owns an object created with make_shared. Improve the design.
Use std::make_unique and transfer ownership explicitly with std::move if ownership changes. Shared ownership is unnecessary here.
Identify the root cause and smallest safe C++23 repair. Explain plainly and precisely.
An externally supplied index is used with vector::operator[]. Repair the boundary.
Validate the index before access. Reject invalid input explicitly, or use at() when exception-based bounds failure is the desired contract.
Identify the root cause and smallest safe C++23 repair. Explain plainly and precisely.
One worker reads a bool while another thread writes it without synchronization.
Use std::atomic_bool for an independent flag, or protect it with the same mutex as the larger invariant it belongs to.
Identify the root cause and smallest safe C++23 repair. Explain plainly and precisely.
A function locks a non-recursive mutex and calls another function that locks the same mutex.
Split the callee into a locked public wrapper and an internal helper requiring the mutex already be held, then call the helper from the first function.
Identify the root cause and smallest safe C++23 repair. Explain plainly and precisely.
Code stores a vector iterator, then push_back may reallocate before the iterator is used.
Do not retain the iterator across a potentially reallocating operation. Reacquire it afterward, use a stable index where valid, or reserve capacity when the size bound is known.
Identify the root cause and smallest safe C++23 repair. Explain plainly and precisely.
Two raw owning pointers are constructed from the same new allocation and both delete it.
Represent the allocation with one owning std::unique_ptr and pass non-owning pointers or references to observers. There must be exactly one deletion responsibility.
Identify the root cause and smallest safe C++23 repair. Explain plainly and precisely.
A polymorphic base is deleted through Base* but Base has a non-virtual destructor.
Give Base a virtual destructor when deletion through the base interface is part of the design, or forbid base-pointer ownership entirely.
Identify the root cause and smallest safe C++23 repair. Explain plainly and precisely.
A detached asynchronous task captures a local variable by reference.
Capture required state by value or move ownership into the task. A detached task must not depend on stack objects whose lifetime may end first.
Identify the root cause and smallest safe C++23 repair. Explain plainly and precisely.
A large size_t is silently converted to int for an API call.
Check that the value fits the target range before converting, then use an explicit cast. Do not rely on implementation-defined truncation or wraparound.
